\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ભાગવું} (bhāgvũ)}{ભાગવું (bhāgvũ)}]{\gu{ભાગવું} (bhāgvũ) — to run away}

\label{lesson:GU-C143-bhagvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to save, then the Gujarati for to sow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ભાગવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ભાગવું}} (\emph{bhāgvũ}) — \textquotedblleft{}to run away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ભાગવું}} (\emph{bhāgvũ}) is a tadbhava. CDIAL lists it under Sanskrit \emph{bhagna}, \textquotedblleft{}broken, defeated\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{bhajyate}, \textquotedblleft{}is broken\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9361). It reports that J. Bloch separated the words meaning \textquotedblleft{}flee\textquotedblright{} from this root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhāgvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bhāgvũ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to save, then the Gujarati for to sow, then say \emph{bhāgvũ} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Describing words — a first pass}

\label{lesson:GU-R143-first-pass-describing-words}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for to believe and to change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item empty, full, true, false, rich
  \item poor, young, strong, weak, necessary
  \item to jump, to swim, to climb, to open, to call
  \item to send, to forget, to look for, to use, to make
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Empty? (\textbf{\gu{ખાલી}}.) Full? (\textbf{\gu{ભરેલું}}.) True? (\textbf{\gu{સાચું}}.) False? (\textbf{\gu{ખોટું}}.) Rich? (\textbf{\gu{અમીર}}.) Poor? (\textbf{\gu{ગરીબ}}.) Young? (\textbf{\gu{જુવાન}}.) Strong? (\textbf{\gu{મજબૂત}}.) Weak? (\textbf{\gu{નબળું}}.) Necessary? (\textbf{\gu{જરૂરી}}.) To jump? (\textbf{\gu{કૂદવું}}.) To swim? (\textbf{\gu{તરવું}}.) To climb? (\textbf{\gu{ચઢવું}}.) To open? (\textbf{\gu{ખોલવું}}.) To call? (\textbf{\gu{બોલાવવું}}.) To send? (\textbf{\gu{મોકલવું}}.) To forget? (\textbf{\gu{ભૂલવું}}.) To look for? (\textbf{\gu{શોધવું}}.) To use? (\textbf{\gu{વાપરવું}}.) To make? (\textbf{\gu{બનાવવું}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[(short timed A1 writing checkpoint)]{A short Gujarati A1 writing checkpoint}

\label{lesson:GU-W10-a1-timed-production}



\begin{quote}
This is a short independent attempt, not a model. You will write the answers, and this page will not show you any copyable Gujarati answer.

Put away romanization, dictionaries, translators, and spell-checkers. Set a \textbf{three-minute timer}. Write in Gujarati script. Short, legible answers are enough.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — timed assessment production}
\textbf{One practical form — three minutes}

Complete \textbf{all six fields in Gujarati script} for a neighbourhood language exchange. Write one short answer in every field. Start the timer when you begin the first field; leave any unfinished field as evidence when it rings.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Your name
  \item Your city or village
  \item A language you speak
  \item One everyday action you do
  \item One drink or food you like
  \item One short question for a new member asking where they live
\end{enumerate}

When the three-minute timer rings, \textbf{stop}. Record the number of completed fields. An honest short attempt is more useful than a perfect untimed one.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Spend at most one minute looking at this first attempt. Note one field you completed clearly and one field to practise next; do not rewrite the timed answer. Keep the page as evidence.

This checkpoint is \textbf{not} the complete A1 writing paper. On another day, close this lesson and open the separate \href{https://github.com/adhithyan15/coding-adventures/blob/main/code/learning/human-languages/gujarati/mocks/a1/writing-paper-1.md}{A1 writing-only learner paper} for the authentic form and named-reader message under one 20-minute assessment clock. That paper and its later rubric review are a separate assessment session, not work inside this under-five-minute lesson. It is writing practice only; it does not establish full A1 exam readiness.
\end{tcolorbox}
